reason: Attacked and survived. I did not take the verifier's reading on trust: I downloaded the page at the Hans Christian Andersen Centre, stripped the markup and read the close of the tale in place. It runs: No costume the Emperor had worn before was ever such a complete success. But he hasn't got anything on, a little child said. Did you ever hear such innocent prattle? said its father. And one person whispered to another what the child had said, He hasn't anything on. A child says he hasn't anything on. But he hasn't got anything on! the whole town cried out at last. The card's wording is that sentence character for character, including got, which is the word the drifted versions lose, and including the full stop rather than the exclamation mark, which belongs to the town's cry four lines later and not to the child. Hersholt prints the speech in double quotation marks; the card renders it in curly singles, which changes no word and follows the house habit already visible in the carry-ins, where 04-fict-08 sets an inner quotation the same way, and which is what the rule against straight double quotes points at anyway. On the edition: the Centre's own page about the translation gives The Complete Andersen, six volumes, New York, 1949, so the translator and year on the card are the Centre's own bibliography and not a guess, and the Limited Editions Club is the publisher of that set. Kejserens nye Klaeder first appeared in Eventyr, fortalte for Boern in 1837, so the dating is right and the line is far inside the 1999 boundary. The locator holds and I checked rather than assumed it: the child speaks during the procession, one sentence after the crowd's praise and four lines before the whole town takes up the cry, with three short paragraphs left in the tale, so at the procession near the close is exact. Attribution is clean, Andersen's own tale, not a proverb and not an anonymous tradition, and although the story descends from an exemplum in El Conde Lucanor the sentence is Andersen's and is the sentence the work is known by. The misattribution list carries nothing for this line; the one Andersen trap in circulation, Where words fail music speaks, which sits in the Calendar For Life candidates as cflId 182, is not this and is not proposed. On the speaker rule: this is a character's line, but the quotation carries its own speech tag, a little child said, so the speaker is named where a reader meets it, and a parenthetical after the locator would repeat the words already inside the quotation. That is the rule satisfied, not the rule dodged. shipped.js: hans christian andersen, no shipped hit, no near hit, zero of three for the year, not banned. Source line form: leads with the name, no dash of any kind, no straight double quote, 113 characters. Tag Fiction is the form of the work. Publishable, and it is the plainest possible picture of the month's theme: a child says what is in front of everybody, and there is no cruelty in it. I could not break it.

residual: Only a typographic choice, not a defect: Hersholt's double quotation marks are rendered as curly singles. If the year's house style ever settles on curly doubles for a speech inside a quotation, this card and 04-fict-08 change together.
